input.title: Why small tools win
input.description: Small, sharp tools outlast sprawling platforms. Here is why.

steps.standardize:
By Mira Okafor on May 14, 2024

Every few years a platform promises to replace the ten tools on your desk with one. It rarely does. The tools that last are the ones that do one thing, expose it cleanly, and stay out of the way.

Composition beats configuration

A pipe between two programs is worth a thousand settings screens. When each piece has a narrow contract, you can swap one without ceremony. The Unix philosophy is a good example, but the principle is older than Unix.

Make each program do one thing well.

The hidden cost of breadth

Breadth has a carrying cost. Every feature is a promise to maintain, document and keep compatible. A small tool makes fewer promises and keeps more of them.

  • Fewer moving parts
  • Faster onboarding
  • Cheaper to replace
cat access.log | grep 500 | sort | uniq -c

None of this means big systems are wrong. It means each addition should earn its place.
